answer: A farm running 32 keys hence pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the ripple stake is held until the nebula settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the ember audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 35% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
